recognition.identity: UCI Online Shoppers Purchasing Intention Dataset (UCI ID 468).
recognition.basis: Identified from the supplied bundle; no independent retrieval or analysis.

candidate.title: How much of the product-page-depth gradient reflects observed session mix?
candidate.question: Among sessions in the lower and upper quartiles of ProductRelated page count, how much does the Revenue-rate difference change after standardizing both groups to the pooled distribution of VisitorType, TrafficType, Month, and Weekend in context cells represented in both groups?

core.object: Session-level Revenue-rate difference between low- and high-ProductRelated-count groups.
core.relation_or_action: Compare the marginal high-minus-low difference with a shared-cell standardized difference, weighting each shared context cell by its pooled group count.
core.contrast: Unadjusted difference versus observed-context-standardized difference among shared cells.
core.prediction: Standardization will attenuate the marginal difference while leaving a positive difference.
core.independent_unit: Session, as described in the supplied metadata.

candidate.failure_condition: The standardized difference is near zero, reversed, or too uncertain to distinguish from zero; or common support is too limited for a useful comparison.
assumptions: The specified context variables capture a useful but incomplete portion of session-composition differences.
Shared-cell standardization describes an observational contrast and does not estimate the effect of causing more product-page views.
Summary fields do not establish whether deeper browsing precedes purchase.
candidate.required_new_data: Dated event-level page sequences to establish temporal ordering, plus independently collected sessions to assess replication and transportability.
candidate.domain_value: Quantifies how much an observed session-depth gradient persists within measured session contexts, informing interpretation of analytics without implying an intervention effect.
candidate.discriminating_delta: Prior proposals tested duration composition, calendar-feature prediction, or other feature associations. This decomposes a low-versus-high page-count outcome difference into marginal and shared-context components and makes overlap part of the estimand.

final.what_changed: The requested computation returned as compute_0. The marginal high-minus-low Revenue-rate difference was 0.1840 (18.40 percentage points); the shared-cell standardized difference was 0.1543 (15.43 points), an attenuation of about 16%. Session-bootstrap 95% intervals were [0.1674, 0.1994] and [0.1356, 0.1775], respectively. There were 181 shared and 167 nonshared context cells; 4.04% of low/high-group sessions were in nonshared cells. All 300 bootstrap replicates were valid. These results support the descriptive contrast in this dataset, not a causal interpretation.
final.what_is_known: ProductRelated quartile cutoffs were 7 and 38; the low and high groups contained 3,156 and 3,106 sessions, with Revenue rates 5.10% and 23.50%. Standardization reduced but did not remove the observed difference. The bootstrap intervals quantify resampling uncertainty under this procedure; they do not account for unmeasured context or establish temporal order. Search result search_1 was limited Crossref metadata and did not establish novelty or rule out direct overlap.
final.new_hypothesis: Measured VisitorType, TrafficType, Month, and Weekend composition accounts for part, but not all, of the product-page-depth Revenue gradient. The remaining difference could reflect other composition, timing, or measurement factors.
final.next_falsifiable_test: Re-estimate the prespecified contrast on independently collected sessions with dated event sequences. Check whether product-page views precede purchase, retain the shared-cell support report, and test whether the standardized difference replicates. A null or reversed replicated contrast would weaken the proposed persistence beyond measured session mix.
final.nearest_work_comparison: The supplied history includes a duration-share comparison conditional on page counts, which asks whether time composition adds predictive information. This candidate instead compares outcome rates across page-count extremes and decomposes their difference by observed context. Returned search metadata covered general purchase prediction and other topics, not this exact decomposition; the search was limited and is not evidence of a literature gap.
final.novelty_status: Unverified. The returned search was not exhaustive and did not confirm a direct match.
